mechanism_narrative: The sharp concurrent fall in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals a broad reduction in out-of-home trips and commuting. That demand loss should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent 4-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below their recent levels for most of the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above its recent baseline, people are spending more time at home and shifting discretionary spending away from shopping districts. That home-centric pattern should depress RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after a residential increase above the stated threshold, or it rises despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates substitution toward local, non-commercial activities and away from shopping trips. When both series rise together, RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days after weeks in which PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both increase together.

mechanism_narrative: A pronounced drop in TRANSIT relative to WORKPLACES indicates access friction or mobility restriction rather than a normal commute shift. That shock should reduce shopping visits almost immediately and keep RETAIL_REC lower for one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points below WORKPLACES for one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the following 7 days after the transit-workplace gap widens past the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained above-baseline PARKS mobility captures seasonal outdoor substitution. If leisure time shifts to parks for several weeks, discretionary retail visits should weaken and RETAIL_REC should trend lower over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days while PARKS stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after a weak week reflects precautionary or necessity shopping that substitutes for discretionary retail trips. If grocery activity recovers while retail access remains soft, RETAIL_REC should decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns up by at least 3 points after a negative week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to weaken within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM turns upward from a prior negative reading.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both keep falling together, commuting-linked foot traffic to commercial areas will keep shrinking. That combined decline should force RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to weaken.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a sustained improvement in WORKPLACES is a leading sign that offices and nearby services are reactivating. That return-to-work channel should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES improving from the snapshot level.
